brief: Goldman's TMT desk frames the morning around ASML's beat: Q3 gross margin hit 57.4%, it raised Q4 GM guidance to 57% and 2026 revenue to €44-45bn, and said 30% annual EUV capacity growth in 2027-28 will not meet customer demand, so it is looking to extend capacity further. Investor feedback was mixed. Against that, semis fell for a fifth session, led by memory and semicap names, as AI sentiment weakened on power and funding constraints, model competition and the risk custom silicon like Microsoft's Maia 300 reduces reliance on Nvidia and AMD. Debt-funded data-centre spending is raising circular-financing and credit-risk concerns, which the desk says is the biggest incremental worry for equity investors. GS's own flow was a 4/10 day with HF buying and LO/tech selling; SPX priced its lowest implied daily move of the year into tomorrow's CPI print. Separately, GS is bullish payments into Q3 (favoring V, MA, TOST, GLBE) and flags UK/EU telecom regulatory fights (Vodafone vs. SpaceX/Amazon spectrum, Netomnia/CMA, Ofcom/Openreach).
